            return cached.value
                    "actor_token": ident.delegated_subject,
        delegated_subject=principal.subject,
checks.note: The process-wide broker caches tokens by audience, scope and tenant, omitting delegated_subject. After user A obtains a token, user B in the same tenant requesting the same audience and scope receives A's cached token without exchanging B's delegated subject. Separate RunIdentity fields therefore do not preserve the launching user's delegation on every call. External STS claim semantics are also unspecified, but the cache bypass is visible locally.

Database grants name an agent-specific database role. Searches across deploy configuration, migrations, release metadata and application code found no STS principal-to-scope bindings, database workload authentication mapping, or external revocation policy. The repo cannot establish that revoking the workload principal alone removes all access independently of users.
